title: Collection: Corralling Your Stuff
coreMove: Capture every loose commitment into visible inboxes before trying to decide or do anything about it.

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital charge nurse starting a double shift with equipment notes, family requests, and staffing concerns arriving at once
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse responsible for keeping a busy ward coordinated
exampleSpecs.stakes: a patient-safety concern or staff handoff detail gets lost because it stayed in her head during interruptions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse stops treating memory as the holding place and drops each loose item into a visible shift inbox before judging priority

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance wedding photographer unpacking camera bags after three weekend shoots
exampleSpecs.audience: a solo creative professional with physical gear, receipts, memory cards, and client promises scattered across bags and email
exampleSpecs.stakes: a client deliverable, expense receipt, or backup step disappears because the work is spread across too many informal hiding places
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the photographer gathers every physical and digital loose end into a few named collection points without editing, sorting, or improving them yet

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent of five-year-old twins clearing the kitchen counter after bedtime
exampleSpecs.audience: a household captain whose mental load mixes school forms, repairs, groceries, and family promises
exampleSpecs.stakes: small obligations keep interrupting sleep and family time because none of them has a reliable place to wait
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the parent writes down every nagging household loop until the mind gets quieter, treating the pile as uncollected stuff rather than personal failure

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender walking from arraignments to client calls with case scraps in pockets and margin notes on folders
exampleSpecs.audience: a lawyer working under time pressure with serious consequences attached to small reminders
exampleSpecs.stakes: a filing date, witness follow-up, or client promise is missed because capture depends on scraps and adrenaline
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the postmortem names the real failure as the absence of a dependable capture habit, then shows a simple portable inbox for every promise made on the move

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional field technician driving between cell towers while receiving parts requests, safety notes, and manager questions
exampleSpecs.audience: a mobile worker whose work arrives while tools, weather, and travel already consume attention
exampleSpecs.stakes: a repair delay or safety report slips because the technician tries to remember it until the next stop
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor keeps asking 'where will that reminder live?' until the technician captures each interruption before returning to the physical job

exampleSpecs.domain: a community theater director one month before opening night with costume fixes, lighting notes, and volunteer conflicts multiplying
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer leader coordinating many small commitments without a formal office system
exampleSpecs.stakes: rehearsals become tense because everyone depends on the director's memory for dozens of unresolved details
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the example contrasts carrying the production in the director's head with making one complete inventory of open loops, showing that collection comes before planning
